clinical_record:
A woman in her 60s presented with numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration. The lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids but flared soon after treatment discontinuation. Some papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk in the past month. No family history of similar lesions was recorded.

Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area without genital involvement. Most lesions were folliculocentric under close inspection. Dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and some foci of structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas with surrounding erythema.

clinical_record:
A man in his 80s was brought to the emergency department after a cardiac arrest. According to paramedics, the patient was last seen healthy by his family 4 hours earlier, then was found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom. He underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, receiving 4 doses of epinephrine intravenously and endotracheal tube intubation with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 10 minutes. Family later revealed he had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had been complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation. A family member witnessed him struggling for air before losing consciousness.

Initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity.

clinical_record:
A 55-year-old white woman with a history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps presented with new-onset flulike symptoms followed by low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques, and 4 weeks of bloody and watery diarrhea. Her facial lesions initially presented as ill-defined pink patches over her cheeks and red papules on her forehead. Over the next 4 days, the lesions spread to her chest, abdomen, back, and left buttock, and a single papule appeared on the right lower extremity. Her low-grade fevers and diarrhea persisted throughout this 4-day period.

In the emergency department, she was febrile and tachycardic. Physical findings included:- 6 × 7-cm well-demarcated vegetative crusted plaques on the bilateral cheeks- Several discrete, round, 1- to 2-cm crusted plaques on the temple- Discrete pustules, vesicles, and umbilicated papules on cheeks and temple- Lesions on chest, abdomen, back, and left buttock- Painful subcutaneous nodules over lower extremities- Polyarthralgia

clinical_record:
A man in his 60s presented with a lesion on the left lower eyelid. His ocular history was notable for a traumatic icicle injury as a child that resulted in loss of the left eye. He had surgery to place an implant into the eye socket, and approximately 14 years prior underwent a lower eyelid reconstruction. He had excellent prosthesis position without need for refitting or replacement for more than 10 years until recently noting that his ocular prosthesis would spontaneously extrude from his anophthalmic socket.

On examination, he had a small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid that had been growing over the past few months. He had contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue across the fornix of the left lower eyelid and increased scleral show of his ocular prosthesis with shortening of his lower eyelid skin. His prosthesis was extruded from his socket due to cicatricial effects causing conjunctival shrinkage and eyelid skin contracture.

- Imaging:  Image Title: Local Recurrence Within Electronic Surface Brachytherapy Field  Image Description: An elevated, pearly lesion on the left lower eyelid with scleral show on the prosthetic eye of the left lateral lower eyelid, showing conjunctival forniceal shortening with extrusion of the prosthesis and cicatricial shortening of the lower eyelid skin- Pathology:  Initial shave biopsy revealed nodular BCC of the left cheek  Subsequent biopsy specimen showed infiltrative pattern with no signs of fibrosis or inflammatory infiltrate
